title: Don't Be a Sucker (1947): how prejudice divided Germany
desc: Don't Be a Sucker is a 1947 U.S. War Department film. It opens on an American street, where a speaker selling a pamphlet turns a crowd against its neighbours, then follows an older man's account of Berlin in 1932: how the Nazis used prejudice as a weapon to divide Germany, what they promised five young men in one crowd, and what those promises came to. Everything said here comes from the film's own narration and dialogue; lines quoted from the film are read in a second voice. The narration voice is synthetic; the archival film is unaltered. Source: U.S. War Department, Educational Film E.F. 6, public domain.
